name: Qwen3.8 27B Q4_K_M on one Intel Arc Pro B70

library.summary: Alibaba's Qwen3.8 27B on one Arc Pro B70 in 4-bit form with llama.cpp, no draft model. The lab's promoted one-card package, rebuilt from pinned source.

featured_metric.label: decode
featured_metric.scope: Conventional 99-interval median on the fixed cold 12-prompt suite; target-only and cache-zero.

contributors.name: neural.download lab
contributors.contribution: Qwen3.8 Q4_K_M bring-up, the complete lab kernel stack, TP1 fusion increments, package, and validation.
contributors.validated_effect: The TP1 matcher and fusion ladder moved the registered 26.047863/26.068073 tok/s baseline to 27.813629/27.824790 tok/s (+6.8% to +7.0%) with 24/24 oracle-exact outputs and the full quality battery passing.

contributors.name: mndodd
contributors.contribution: Optimized Intel SYCL llama.cpp fork used as the pinned runtime base beneath the lab's Qwen3.8 patch stack.
contributors.validated_effect: On the separate matched Qwen3.6 Q8 TP2 control, the fork measured 31.338765 vs 29.610651 tok/s (+5.836%); that A/B does not assign the later Qwen3.8 package result to the fork.

known_limitations: The package launch is one slot at 8K. A separate oneAPI 2026.1.1 audit loaded 64 slots at 512 nominal tokens per slot, but used 32281.7/32656 MiB and failed batch-shape exact-output and point-order stability gates; its 86.28/85.97 tok/s rows are diagnostic only, so the HTTP concurrency curve remains pending.
Qwen3.8 27B is dense; do not compare this one-card aggregate rate as if it were a sparse Qwen-derived MoE or an NVIDIA NVFP4 deployment.

project_patches.reason: The one-card speed and exactness identity depends on the lab's complete source stack and TP1 matcher increments.

commands.stop: Ctrl-C in the foreground server terminal; then pgrep -x llama-server must return no process
